purpose: concepts the domain reviewers found with no card, no pending entry and an openable source: each is a research run to queue (a topic object of one or two candidate rules for scripts/research-topic-workflow.js), never a hand-written card (HANDOVER 5.8)

runs.concept: A series is presented in final form, with fix-up commits folded into the commit they fix
runs.claim: squash fix-up and reviewer-feedback commits so only the end state remains; keep layered commits; checkable on the commit list base..head

runs.concept: Deliberate debt is taken on only for a hard deadline or an emergency, never for a soft deadline
runs.claim: most deadlines are soft; code health is not sacrificed for them; checkable only against a change description that invokes urgency

runs.concept: Deep nesting: a block nested too deeply inside its routine (CC19 "Taming Dangerously Deep Nesting"). The design note computes a `deep_nesting` signal ("the block depth of an added line inside its routine ... depth of 4 or more") but no card's triggers name it; pending entry 69 holds composite complexity scores, not a nesting-depth bound.
runs.claim: "Many developers consider code difficult to read if blocks are nested beyond a certain depth."; "This rule enforces a maximum depth that blocks can be nested to reduce code complexity."; `"max"` (default `4`)

runs.concept: Complex boolean expressions: a condition built from many boolean operators, not broken into named parts (CC19 "Boolean Expressions"); CODE-82 covers only comparison with true/false.
runs.claim: "Restricts the number of boolean operators (&&, ||, &, | and ^) in an expression."; "Rationale: Too many conditions leads to code that is difficult to read"

runs.concept: Division by a divisor that can be zero (CC12 "Anticipate divide-by-zero errors"); CODE-30's Limits put "division by zero" outside the rule and no other card or pending entry holds it.
runs.claim: "If the divisor is zero at run time, a run-time panic occurs." (a curl of SonarSource/sonar-java sonar-java-plugin/src/main/resources/org/sonar/l10n/java/rules/java/S3518.html returned no such text, so that rule is not cited)

runs.concept: Exact decimal quantities (money) held in binary floating point (CC12): CODE-31's Limits defer it ("Whether a quantity that must be exact, such as money, belongs in binary floating point at all ... are judged by their own rules") and CODE-27's Limits put "the choice of a decimal type for decimal quantities" outside, but no card or pending entry holds it.
runs.source_path: python/cpython Doc/library/decimal.rst (opening list of the decimal module's advantages)
runs.claim: "The exactness carries over into arithmetic. In decimal floating point, ``0.1 + 0.1 + 0.1 - 0.3`` is exactly equal to zero."; "decimal is preferred in accounting applications which have strict ..." (equality invariants)
